Definition: from G1722 and G4429; to spit at or on:--spit (upon).
BiblicalUsage: To spit on someone is the lowest contempt, and Jesus took it. He says He will be mocked and spitted on in Luke 18:32, the soldiers spit in His face and buffet Him in Matthew 26:67, and in Mark 14:65 they cover His face and strike Him and say, Prophesy.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe there is no depth of shame Christ did not taste for us — He let men spit in the face of God, and answered with silence. I hold that when I am treated with contempt for His sake, I am sharing the smallest part of what He bore, and He counts it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
